questions.q: Which field would be the most suitable primary key in a table of students?
questions.why: A primary key must be unique for every record; only the student ID is.

questions.q: Which data type is best for a field that stores whether a book has been returned (yes or no)?
questions.why: Two possible values, TRUE or FALSE, is a Boolean field.

questions.q: A table Car has fields Make and Price. Which query counts how many cars are made by Ford?
options: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Car WHERE Make = "Ford";
SELECT SUM(Make) FROM Car WHERE Ford;
SELECT Make FROM Car ORDER BY COUNT;
questions.why: COUNT(*) with FROM and a WHERE condition returns the number of matching records.

questions.q: Explain what a primary key is and why a table needs one.
questions.model: A primary key is a field whose value is unique for every record. It allows each record to be identified without confusion and stops duplicate records being stored.
points: Field with a unique value for each record
